issue.title: test_all_tab_help_guides_show_forward_jump_and_agents_metadata_sections is over the flake baseline with no bead, blocking check-full's last gate
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-u6 land agent while discharging phase bead sase-u6.4's note 1, which
asked the land agent to confirm that sase-u7 and its siblings cover the current
flake-baseline red set before landing epic sase-u6. They do not: the gate now reports 9
nodes over baseline, not the 7 sase-u6.4 measured, and this node is one of two with no
bead. NOT caused by sase-u6: that epic adds Artifacts pane descriptions, a pane brief,
sub-tab tooltips and PNG goldens, and every failure record for this node predates its
first commit.

`just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake` is the last gate of `just check-full`, so an
undeclared node here blocks every landing agent that reaches it.

The node is a pure synchronous registry assertion with no I/O, async, or timing --
`load_keymap_registry({})` followed by set membership checks on the CLS, Agents, and AXE
help-guide binding tables. There is nothing in the test itself that can race, which
points at process-global state leaking in from another test under the parallel lane
rather than at anything local. That is the class in-progress epic sase-j7 exists to fix
by mechanism.

The other unbeaded node from the same gate run,
tests/ace/tui/test_artifacts_scaffold.py::test_subtab_strip_labels_and_accents_cover_all_panes,
is a different situation and was routed to sase-o0 instead: it was a true deterministic
failure caused by 4dd299502 and fixed by 179508566, so all of its evidence is stale
pre-fix and it needs a `# fixed-at:` declaration, not a flake bead.

task_type_fields.evidence: 12 failure records in the durable selection-health store, all recorded 2026-08-25 between 21:48Z and 23:07Z across three distinct trees (f56cf433328e, 79e51b564ec9, 012a66a65985), so it is not a single bad run. Passes serially at HEAD 8d074c8dd (1 passed, 2.19s). It did NOT fail in either of the two most recent full-lane records (20260826T122413Z and 20260826T122507Z, tree c8a3c606871e), which is why it presents as intermittent rather than deterministic. Fails only under the full parallel lane; no entry in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt. The only commit touching tests/test_keymaps_display_help.py or src/sase/ace/tui/keymaps/ after the last failing tree is ceaa377fe, which only adds three keymap entries and does not modify this test, so no fix has been identified and the node cannot be retired as already-fixed evidence.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake (gate report); .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_keymaps_display_help.py::test_all_tab_help_guides_show_forward_jump_and_agents_metadata_sections passes serially in 2.19s

payload.description: Same gate, same landing-blocking failure mode: sase-u7 was filed for the one node over the flake baseline with no bead, and this is the next such node found when the set grew from 7 to 9.

A pure synchronous keymap-registry assertion with nothing local to race, so it likely belongs to the process-global-state leak class this epic fixes by mechanism; check its leak detector covers the keymap registry first.
